The Quality Management Department reports to the Medical Center Director and is responsible for providing an impartial and forthright review of the entire Medical Center's preparation and performance for accreditation reviews and overall quality of patient care to the Medical Center's executive leadership.

The Accreditation Specialist (AS) reports to the Deputy Director of Quality Management and is accountable to the Director of Quality Management.

The AS promotes the medical center mission, vision, and values, complies with the Equal Employment Opportunity programs, partnerships, customer service standards and Veterans Affairs policies and procedures and works with internal and external customers to the Quality Management Department to support these goals and successes.

Collaborates with leadership and colleagues to complete all other duties as assigned.

The Accreditation Program requirements include, but are not limited to, developing and coordinating internal review systems to assure that both clinical and administrative programs follow agency and accrediting standards and regulatory requirements, utilizes databases to improve performance and outcome measures, identifying trends and opportunities for improvement in performance and collaborating with the clinicians throughout the Medical Center to understand the processes that support the metrics and how to develop improvement plans for sustainment of those metrics.

The AS is responsible for translating regulatory and accrediting body standards, policies, and strategies into action within the complex interrelationships that exist in a health care environment as it applies to program oversight areas.

The Quality Management Accreditation Nurse contributes to the overall success of the Quality Management Department by providing expert oversight and direction on all accreditation program activities, which includes preparation and post-review improvement activities through collaborating and providing feedback on any clinical or administrative practice or process within the Medical Center surrounding program requirements and alignment with the numerous accreditation organizations who provide oversight for the organization.

The Quality Management Accreditation Nurse is expected to be self-directed and self-managing in performance of their daily activities. The Quality Management Accreditation Nurse serves as a liaison, representing the facility accreditation program, to the Veterans Integrated System Network (VISN).

The AS serves as the primary point of contact for VISN requests and participates in VISN activities. The AS is required to communicate and maintain positive relationships with other departments and agencies, both within and outside of the Lebanon VAMC.

The Care Manager Registered Nurse responsibility is to demonstrates integration of biopsychosocial concepts, cognitive skills, and technically competent practice while providing care to clients. Assesses, plans, implements, and evaluates the effectiveness of the Veteran's care.

Serves to support delivery of high quality, timely care to the Veteran receiving services in the community.

Assumes responsibility for the coordination of care focused on patient education, self-management, and customer satisfaction throughout the continuum of care to include other duties but are not limited to: The Care Manager possesses intimate knowledge of the internal referral care process, clinical review criteria, utilization management standards, clinical documentation requirements, community care regulations, and Veterans Health Administration (VHA) standards and guidelines.

The Care Manager uses nursing knowledge and systems theory to assess, organize, facilitate, and guide Veterans through their full range of care options including internal/direct care in Veterans Affairs (VA) and care in the community.

The Care Manager serves as a liaison to both internal and community providers and is responsible for managing the care of the Veteran throughout the consult process.

The Care Manager supports the medical center's mission to improve timely access to care, ensure Veterans who want to receive care in the community are referred and scheduled into the community, and support the delivery of high quality, timely care to the Veteran receiving community services.

The Care Manager will work collaboratively within the Office of Integrated Veteran Care (IVC) to triage Request for Services (RFS) to coordinate care processes defined by the IVC Field Guidebook to include developing a care coordination plan, reviewing medical documentation from community providers, communication of care coordination needs, and supporting the Veteran through the completion of the episode of care.

The Care Manager will influence care outcomes by collaborating with members of the interdisciplinary team both within the VA and in the community. The Care Manager will comply with VA-mandated processes and use of health information solutions that serve to assess, document, exchange, and track care coordination information.

The Care Manager will utilize delegation of authority, if applicable, to function at their highest level of role performance and align high-quality care with key performance indicators to ensure practice standards meet patient care needs.

Duties and Responsibilities include but are not limited to: Provides administrative and clinical leadership for the Referral Coordination Program (RCP), ensuring effective coordination of referral management activities across the organization.

Oversees the coordination, implementation, and continuous improvement of clinical referral management processes to ensure timely, appropriate, and Veteran-centered care.

Serves as the liaison between Surgery Service, specialty providers, nursing staff, administrative personnel, and leadership to facilitate efficient referral coordination and communication.

Supervises nursing and clinical staff by planning work assignments, establishing priorities, monitoring workload distribution, and ensuring efficient daily operations.

Ensures nursing care and referral management activities comply with Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Office of Community Care (OCC), accreditation, regulatory, and professional practice standards.

Leads quality improvement initiatives by analyzing referral management data, monitoring program performance metrics, identifying trends, and recommending operational improvements.

Develops, revises, and implements standard operating procedures, policies, and workflows in response to changes in national directives, OCC guidance, VISN requirements, and facility policies. Collaborates with physicians, specialty consultants, and interdisciplinary teams to improve clinical coordination, referral processes, and patient outcomes.

Reviews clinical documentation to ensure compliance with Referral Coordination Initiative requirements, regulatory standards, and organizational policies. Monitors program performance through data analysis, prepares reports and presentations, and provides recommendations to executive leadership for process improvement.

Recruits, interviews, selects, mentors, and develops staff while collaborating with Human Resources to support timely hiring and workforce planning. Evaluates employee performance by establishing expectations, conducting competency assessments, completing performance evaluations, and providing ongoing coaching and feedback.

Identifies staff educational needs and coordinates orientation, continuing education, competency validation, and mandatory training to support professional development and regulatory compliance.

Addresses employee relations matters by resolving workplace concerns, counseling staff, recommending disciplinary actions when appropriate, and ensuring adherence to labor relations and Equal Employment Opportunity requirements.

Ensures exceptional customer service by promoting Veteran-centered care, improving patient satisfaction, and supporting safe, respectful, and equitable healthcare delivery.

Maintains operational readiness by monitoring compliance with accreditation standards, patient safety initiatives, infection prevention practices, and organizational performance requirements.

Performs referral management and clinical review activities to maintain subject matter expertise, identify operational barriers, and support efficient patient access to specialty care.

Participates in facility, VISN, and interdisciplinary committees, task forces, and workgroups to advance nursing practice, referral coordination, and organizational initiatives. Analyzes current and future workforce requirements to determine staffing needs, competency requirements, and resource allocation to meet program objectives.

Provides leadership coverage for senior Referral Coordination Program management as assigned and performs other related duties necessary to support organizational and patient care objectives.

Participer à l’organisation et à la répartition des activités au sein de l’équipe.
Contribuer à l’utilisation efficiente et optimale des ressources.

Documenter les soins, transmissions et actions de coordination.
Préparer et transmettre les dossiers médicaux avec l’ensemble des documents requis.
Assurer les communications par téléphone, e-mail, courrier et outils de communication internes.
Participer à l’accueil des patients et à l’orientation des demandes.
Effectuer les tâches administratives nécessaires au bon déroulement de la prise en charge.

Participer à la prévention des infections et à la sécurité des patients.

Participer au développement et à l’harmonisation des pratiques professionnelles.
Contribuer au projet de service en collaboration avec la responsable et la coordinatrice des soins.
Participer au partage des connaissances, à l’accompagnement et à l’évaluation des compétences des membres de l’équipe.
